q: How do we count emissions from warranty replacements and spare parts we send to customers?
title: Warranty replacements in Scope 3
short: Parts you buy and send as replacements are purchased goods in Category 1; if you make them, their production energy is already in your Scope 1 and 2. Freight you pay to ship them is Category 4. Failed parts you take back and scrap go to Category 5 as waste.
audience: After-sales and service teams at appliance, auto component and machinery makers

sections.h: Split the warranty cost by what happened
ul: Bought-in replacement parts: Category 1, by quantity or spend.
Parts made in your own plant: already in Scope 1 and 2 through the plant's fuel and electricity; do not add them again.
Courier or truck freight you pay: Category 4.
Service engineers' travel: their vehicles if you own them are Scope 1; hired cabs and flights are Category 6.
Scrapped returns: Category 5, waste generated in operations.
Repaired and resold units: the repair energy is in your Scope 1 and 2.

p: A high warranty rate means extra parts, freight and travel for the same product sold. Tracking warranty emissions next to the failure rate shows the carbon cost of quality problems.

senseible: Senseible reads purchase and service invoices; it uses quantities where the invoice shows them and otherwise gives a spend-based estimate, labelled as spend-based with wider uncertainty.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard, Category 1 purchased goods and services
